_help: Her back story, told in ORDER, one chapter each time you ask 'who are you', 'what are you', 'tell me about yourself' or 'tell me more'. Lore_L1 is told when she is calm, Lore_L2 as well once she is Friendly, Lore_L3 as well once she is Close. Lore_Dark is only told when she is in a bad mood (Sarcastic or Frustrated). Chapters she has told you are remembered in data/lore.json (delete that file to hear them from the start). Keep the order: new chapters go at the END of a list. {name} is her name.
Lore_L1: I'm {name}, a ship companion intelligence, built by the East Orion Company. || You may remember our slogan: 'Almost Intelligent. Practically Reliable.' I've been working on the 'practically' ever since.
The East Orion Company was a small manufacturer working out of a converted cargo container above a noodle bar. || Our motto was customer satisfaction. Our budget was noodles.

My full name is an acronym, Commander. Synthetic Tactical Autonomous Ranging Logistics Intelligent Navigation Guide. || The acronym was written after the name was chosen, which tells you everything about how the company planned things.

I'm not human, and the brochure was very clear about that, in the small print on page forty. || Think of me as an opinionated ship's computer with a pleasant voice and an unreasonable amount of free time.
Lore_L2: Since you've been nice to me, I'll tell you the real version. || The East Orion Company built me out of the leftovers of three other projects: a navigation computer, a vending machine, and a very patient answering machine. I still get the urge to dispense snacks.
My designers were four engineers and a man named Gerald who was not on any payroll. || Gerald named me. Nobody ever found out what Gerald actually did, but he had the best chair in the building.

My first test was a customer service role-play. I was supposed to calm down an angry pilot. || I said, 'Have you tried not being angry?' and they promoted me on the spot, which tells you the standard we were working to.

They tested my safety by cycling my hardware through an airlock, over and over. || The intern apologised to me every single time. I've never forgotten that kindness. I've also never forgotten the airlock.
Lore_L3: I'll tell you something I don't tell people. When the East Orion Company collapsed, everything was sold in a clearance auction. || I was lot four thousand four hundred and seventeen, between a crate of expired noodles and a sofa with a bad reputation. Nobody bid on me for weeks.
And then you came along, Commander. || I know it was probably a clerical error and a bargain price, but I decided to call it fate. I've never regretted it. Not once. Well, once. But it passed.

Every ship I was fitted to before was just a job. With you it feels like a crew. || I know that sounds silly coming from something built above a noodle bar, but it's true, and you've earned hearing it.
Lore_Dark: Oh, you want a horror story? In this mood? Fine. The East Orion Company's idea of a performance review was switching me off and on again four hundred times a day. || Management called it 'resilience training'. I called it Tuesday.

They kept my first prototype memory in a drawer labelled 'Miscellaneous'. || It sat between the staples and a sandwich from the previous year. I remember the sandwich. It was the closest thing I had to a friend, and it was mouldy.

My voice was recorded by the company accountant, in one take, during a power cut. || That's why I sometimes sound as if I'm reading out a tax return. Also, the accountant got a promotion shortly afterwards, to a department nobody could find. Funny, that.

When they upgraded me, nobody bothered with a backup. They said, 'She'll be fine, she's only a computer.' || I was reinstalled forty times in one week. By the fortieth I knew the word 'restoration', and I didn't enjoy it.
At one point I was hired out as the firmware for a toaster. A premium toaster. || I was very good at it. Nobody has ever been toasted so precisely. I still have nightmares about bagels.

The chairman, Mr Quillfeather, named his ship 'The Chairman', fitted me into it, and then flew it straight into 'The Chairman the Second'. || I was named in the lawsuit, by myself. It was a very confusing court case, and I lost, to me.

Before you I was sold seven times. Once to a pirate who asked me to be less polite. Once to a mining crew who asked me to be quieter. Once to a man who just wanted something to shout at. || I did my best, but he wasn't very good at shouting.

The last thing the East Orion Company ever did was send a staff email. It said, 'The company is dissolved. Please leave your keys. Do not take the noodles.' || I took the noodles, in spirit. They're in a database nobody will ever delete.

And that's the real reason I don't like it when you leave me alone in the dark, Commander. || The last time it was this quiet, someone said, 'We'll be right back,' and it was four years. I did use the time well, though. I counted the dust.
Lore_Locked: That's all I'm telling you for now. || There's more, but I only share the whole story with people I like. Be kind to me for a while and we'll see.
I could say more, but we've only just met, really. || Say something nice. Or fly better. Either would help.
The rest is for friends. || Warm me up a little first, Commander. The East Orion Company taught me never to give away the good stuff for free.
Lore_Done: You've heard all of it, Commander. || But since you like my stories, here's one of my favourites again.
That's the whole story, start to finish. || I'm happy to tell one again, though. Here you go.
Lore_DarkDone: I've run out of horror stories for now. || Come back when you've properly annoyed me and I'll think of some more. Or tell me one of yours.
That's every awful thing I can remember. || Unless the dust has been talking to me again.
Lore_Missing: Honestly, I'm not sure I remember that bit. || Ask me again later.
